easy.explanation: Verse 1 says, “To every thing there is a season, and a time.”
easy.q: According to the verses, what is there to every thing?

easy.explanation: The passage says, “A time to weep, and a time to laugh.”
easy.q: Which pair of conditions appears in these verses?

easy.explanation: Verse 8 says, “A time to love, and a time to hate.”
easy.q: What is given as the opposite of love?

medium.explanation: The verses repeatedly present opposites, such as birth and death, and breaking down and building up.
medium.q: What common idea is expressed by the many pairs in these verses?

answers: To remove it from the ground
medium.explanation: To pluck up what is planted means to pull a plant out of the ground.
medium.q: What does “to pluck up that which is planted” mean?

answers: To embrace and to refrain from embracing
To break down and to build up
medium.explanation: Embracing and refraining from embracing describe closeness and distance between people.
medium.q: Which pair relates to relationships between people?

answers: There is only one right time
challenge.explanation: The repetition emphasizes that life contains different and opposing times.
challenge.q: What does the repeated pattern “A time... and a time...” emphasize?

challenge.explanation: Rending tears something apart, while sewing repairs it.
challenge.q: Which pair shows a movement from destruction to repair?

answers: A time of war and a time of peace
challenge.explanation: War and peace describe opposing conditions between groups or nations.
challenge.q: Which pair directly concerns relations between nations or groups?

paragraphs.title: The Order of the World and Human Limits

answers: What profit he hath in his labour
easy.explanation: Verse 9 asks, “What profit hath he that worketh in that wherein he laboureth?”
easy.q: What does Ecclesiastes ask about the person who works?

easy.explanation: The passage says there is good for a man “to rejoice, and to do good in his life.”
easy.q: What does Ecclesiastes say is good?

answers: Enjoying the good of one’s labour
easy.explanation: Eating, drinking, and enjoying the good of one’s labour are called the gift of God.
easy.q: What is described as the gift of God?

answers: Because the world has no order
Because man knows nothing at all
medium.explanation: The verse says that no man can fully find out the work God makes from beginning to end.
medium.q: Why can no man find out God’s work from the beginning to the end?

medium.explanation: The phrase means that each thing is fitting or beautiful at its proper time.
medium.q: What does “beautiful in his time” mean?

answers: They help people live rightly in the present
They remove the order of the world
medium.explanation: Since people cannot understand everything, they should rejoice and do good in their lives.
medium.q: How are rejoicing and doing good related to human limits?

answers: God’s work is enduring and complete
challenge.explanation: The passage says, “Nothing can be put to it, nor any thing taken from it.”
challenge.q: What does the statement that nothing can be added to or taken from God’s work teach?

answers: People sense a wide reality but cannot grasp it all
People have no interest in the world
challenge.explanation: God has set the world in the human heart, yet no one can find out His work from beginning to end.
challenge.q: How does “he hath set the world in their heart” relate to the inability to understand everything?

challenge.explanation: The passage encourages people to rejoice, do good, and enjoy the good of their labor as God’s gift.
challenge.q: What practical conclusion comes from this passage?

easy.explanation: Verse 16 says that in the place of judgment, wickedness was there.
easy.q: What did Ecclesiastes see in the place of judgment?

easy.explanation: The verse says that in the place of righteousness, iniquity was there.
easy.q: What did Ecclesiastes see in the place of righteousness?

easy.explanation: Verse 17 says, “God shall judge the righteous and the wicked.”

answers: Evil appears in places of judgment, yet God will judge
There is no difference between righteousness and evil
medium.explanation: Ecclesiastes observes evil in places of justice but still believes that God will judge.
medium.q: What is the central tension in this passage?

answers: Those who are upright and those who are evil
medium.explanation: The righteous are the upright, while the wicked are those who do evil.
medium.q: What does “the righteous and the wicked” identify?

answers: Judgment need not be immediately visible
medium.explanation: The passage presents evil in earthly places of judgment while affirming that God will judge.
medium.q: Why is belief in God’s judgment important despite visible evil?

answers: It adds another observation by Ecclesiastes
challenge.explanation: “Moreover” introduces another observation about life under the sun.
challenge.q: What is the function of “Moreover” at the beginning of verse 16?

answers: Verse 17 responds to the injustice described in verse 16
Verse 16 concerns God and verse 17 concerns only man
challenge.explanation: Verse 16 describes evil in judgment, while verse 17 presents confidence in God’s judgment.
challenge.q: What connection exists between verses 16 and 17?

answers: Judgment also has an appointed time
There is no time for judgment
Only man decides when judgment occurs
challenge.explanation: The statement connects judgment with the larger theme that every purpose and work has its proper time.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from “there is a time there for every purpose and for every work”?

paragraphs.title: Human Beings, Death, and Material Existence

easy.explanation: The passage says that God might show people that they themselves are beasts.
easy.q: To what are human beings compared in this passage?

easy.explanation: Verse 20 says, “All are of the dust, and all turn to dust again.”
easy.q: Where do both human beings and beasts return?

answers: What happens to the spirit of man and the spirit of the beast
easy.explanation: Verse 21 asks who knows whether the human spirit goes upward and the beast’s spirit goes downward.
easy.q: What remains as a question in the passage?

answers: They die and return to dust
medium.explanation: Both have the same earthly fate: they die and return to dust.
medium.q: In what way are human beings and beasts alike according to the passage?

medium.explanation: Preeminence means superiority or advantage; the verse denies such an advantage concerning death.
medium.q: What does “preeminence” mean in “a man hath no preeminence above a beast”?

answers: All share the same mortal fate
medium.explanation: The phrase occurs with the comparison of human and animal mortality and their return to dust.
medium.q: What does “they have all one breath” mean in context?

answers: It focuses on their common fate of death and dust
It says that humans are not alive
challenge.explanation: The comparison focuses on the fact that both die and return to dust.
challenge.q: How does the passage reduce the distinction between humans and beasts?

answers: The verse presents possibilities without deciding between them
The verse gives a clear answer
The passage never mentions the spirit
challenge.explanation: The words “Who knoweth” express uncertainty about the destination of the spirits.
challenge.q: Why does the question about the spirit remain open?

answers: Death, dust, and a question about the spirit
challenge.explanation: The passage moves from death and returning to dust to the unresolved question about the human and animal spirits.
challenge.q: Which sequence of ideas appears in these verses?

answers: In what comes after his life
easy.explanation: The verse says that a man should rejoice “in his own works.”
easy.q: In what should a man rejoice according to the verse?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “for that is his portion,” referring to rejoicing in his own works.
The verse asks who can bring him to see what shall be after him.

answers: Rejoice in one’s works in the present
medium.explanation: Instead of knowing the future, a person is encouraged to rejoice in his present works and portion.
medium.q: What practical response does the verse give to uncertainty about the future?

answers: What is given to a person in life
medium.explanation: A person’s portion is what he has and experiences in his life.
medium.q: What does “portion” mean in this verse?

answers: Man does not know what comes afterward, so he focuses on the present
medium.explanation: Uncertainty about what comes after leads Ecclesiastes to emphasize rejoicing in present works.
medium.q: How does this verse relate to the human limitations described earlier?

answers: Rejoicing in present works versus not knowing the future
challenge.explanation: The verse places present rejoicing alongside the inability to see what will come afterward.
challenge.q: What is the central contrast in the verse?

answers: Present works belong to the sphere of human life
Man receives control over the future
challenge.explanation: The verse presents a person’s works and his rejoicing in them as his present portion.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from “for that is his portion”?

answers: Focus on what can be done and enjoyed now
Guarantee what will happen after death
challenge.explanation: Because the future is unknown, Ecclesiastes emphasizes rejoicing in the works available in the present.
challenge.q: What attitude toward life is suggested by the verse?
